title: POC Weekly - Latency Tuning (Rivermark)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency benchmarks and next tuning steps. Customer shared updated TTFT numbers for two models and constraints for private deployment. Redwood SE recommended streaming configuration, prefix caching and kernel sweep. Agreed next steps: run kernel sweep with 4k sequences, test streaming + chunked responses, and share updated benchmark sheet. Security asked for clarifications on audit logs and KMS usage.
next_steps: Samir to run kernel-sweep (fp16 / int8 / cuda-optimized kernels) for 4k seq by 2028-05-17 and share results
Jordan to send updated POC pricing and config doc (streaming + canary) by 2028-05-12
Priya to review and confirm KMS/SOC2 artifacts, Redwood to share security pack link by 2028-05-14
action_items: Samir Patel - run kernel sweep across candidate kernels (cuda, fused attention, quantized int8) for sequence lengths 512/2048/4096 - due 2028-05-17
Jordan Lee - send POC pricing + streaming config + example curl commands - due 2028-05-12
Elena Ruiz - update benchmark sheet with latest TTFT numbers and share link - due 2028-05-12
Priya Shah (RiverMark) - confirm KMS/HSM constraints and what audit logs they need - due 2028-05-14
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we'll get started. Anita, thanks for making time.
[00:06] Anita Gomez: Yeah thanks, Jordan. Quick note, we've got Mark and Priya on in case infra or security questions come up.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: Great. Agenda: quick benchmark review, TTFT numbers, streaming behavior, kernel choices, then next steps. Samir, can you take us through the numbers?
[00:23] Samir Patel: Sure. So we re-ran the microbench yesterday with the 7B variant and a trimmed 13B floating point baseline. Observed TTFT on hosted endpoint ~180ms median for 512 tokens when using batching disabled; with streaming enabled the first token drops to ~95ms but end-to-end increases slightly because of chunking overhead.
[00:44] Mark Reynolds: Wait, 95ms first token? That's good. What's your payload size and chunk size for streaming?
[00:49] Samir Patel: We sent a typical prompt ~120 tokens; chunk size configured to 64 tokens per chunk. We saw diminishing returns past chunk size 32 for TTFT because of serialization.
[01:02] Leo Tan: And what about longer sequences? We need to support some analytic summaries up to 4k.
[01:07] Samir Patel: Right - with 2048 tokens median latency grows predictably, TTFT moves to ~220ms on the same config; for 4096 it's ~400-430ms first token if no prefix caching. With prefix/KV caching enabled for stable contexts we saw 40-60% reduction on repeated prefixes.
[01:28] Anita Gomez: Our main concern is the tail - 95th/99th percentile. Can you share p95 numbers?
[01:33] Samir Patel: p95 for the 512 run was ~420ms without streaming; with streaming p95 dropped to ~300ms for first token, but total completion p95 remained higher for long outputs. We included CPU and GPU utilization columns in the sheet.
[01:47] Mark Reynolds: One of our constraints is private deployment in our VPC; network hops and proxy add ~60-80ms baseline. Have you accounted for that?
[01:55] Samir Patel: We ran a simulated VPC network profile - you should expect added baseline. Our recommendation: for RiverMark, Dedicated nodes in same region + streaming will get you under 200ms TTFT for common short prompts.
[02:10] Priya Shah: Security question - when you mention prefix caching and KV, are any customer tokens or PII stored? We need to understand retention and KMS handling.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: Good callout. By default we don't persist PII in cache; caching is managed in-memory on the serving nodes and can be disabled. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS for key material and audit logs. We'll share the security pack.
[02:35] Priya Shah: Okay please send the SOC2 and KMS docs. Also any intel on RBAC and SAML provisioning and whether logs are exported to our SIEM.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: We'll include RBAC/SAML playbook and a short note on CloudTrail/Datadog export options.
[02:52] Samir Patel: Back to tuning - kernel choice made a big delta. On A100 GPUs the fused-attention kernel reduced per-token latency by ~12% versus default cuDNN for our 13B baseline; on older V100-class hardware the int8 quantized kernel helps more but note some quality drop.
[03:12] Anita Gomez: How big is the quality drop for int8? We have sensitive customer-facing copy so hallucination changes matter.
[03:19] Samir Patel: In our tests with 100 eval prompts, int8 produced minor divergence in ~7% of cases compared to fp16; depends heavily on prompt distribution. We recommend baseline evals tied to your prompt set before rolling int8 into production.
[03:33] Leo Tan: Can we run a kernel-sweep? Try fused attention, windowed attention, and int8 on our representative queries.
[03:40] Samir Patel: Yes - that's queued as an action item. We'll run across seq lengths 512/2048/4096 and provide latency/quality tradeoff metrics.
[03:49] Mark Reynolds: Also curious if batch size tuning helps TTFT - often batching helps throughput but hurts first token. Any tips?
[03:55] Samir Patel: For your latency SLOs, set continuous batching threshold low or use adaptive batching with per-tenant latency caps; for TTFT-sensitive endpoints we suggest batch size 1 with streaming on, and for high-throughput less-latency-sensitive paths increase batch window. We can provide config snippets.
[04:14] Anita Gomez: Any immediate wins we should apply?
[04:18] Samir Patel: Yes - enable streaming + chunk size 32, enable prefix caching for repeated flows, and test fused-attn kernel on your instance. Also consider quantization on a canary model to measure quality drift.
[04:32] Priya Shah: On audit logs - do you keep per-token logs or only request-level metadata?
[04:36] Jordan Lee: We retain request-level metadata by default. Full token logs are opt-in and can be routed to your SIEM under strict retention policies; for Private you'll control retention via your own S3/Blob with lifecycle rules.
[04:50] Mark Reynolds: For the POC, what's the simplest config to get streaming + low TTFT in our VPC?
[04:56] Jordan Lee: Dedicated node in the same AZ, streaming enabled, chunk size 32, batch window 10ms, prefix caching - that'll be our recommended starting point. We'll include exact helm/terraform snippets in the doc.
[05:12] Anita Gomez: Timeline - we'd like 2 weeks of tests and then a decision point. Can we aim to have the kernel results and updated benchmark sheet by next Wed?
[05:20] Jordan Lee: Yes, Samir will run the sweep and Elena will update the sheet. We'll follow up next Wed.
[05:27] Priya Shah: Also need the SOC2 and KMS/keys whitepaper before then.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: We'll send that as part of the security pack.
[05:35] Samir Patel: One more technical note - TTFT improvements are often not linear with sequence length; the write patterns (prefix heavy vs generated-free) change KV cache hit-rates. We'll include a small script you can run to measure your own distributions.
[05:49] Anita Gomez: Perfect. Thank you, everyone. Recap?
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Quick recap: Samir runs kernel sweep by 2028-05-17; Jordan sends pricing and streaming config by 2028-05-12; Elena updates sheet and shares link; Priya reviews KMS items; follow-up on 2028-05-17. Any other questions?
[06:07] Mark Reynolds: None from infra.
[06:09] Priya Shah: All good.
[06:11] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, wrap up.
notes: Benchmark sheet referenced: (link redacted) - 'rivermark-poc-benchmarks.csv'. Security pack link to be shared via email. Some transcription errors likely in technical kernel names and exact ms values.
